shopify.title: Connect Shopify
shopify.intro: Two ways: a custom app created in the store admin (fastest, one store) or a public app with OAuth (one install flow for every customer).

steps.title: Create the custom app
steps.body: In the store admin open Settings → Apps and sales channels → Develop apps → Create an app. Name it “Keel”.

steps.title: Grant Admin API scopes
steps.body: In Configuration → Admin API integration select the scopes listed on the right for the modules the customer bought. Save.

steps.title: Install and copy the token
steps.body: Install the app, then reveal the Admin API access token once (shpat_…) and the API secret key. Paste both in Keel → Integrations → Shopify → Connect. Keel stores them encrypted (AES-GCM).

steps.title: Webhooks
steps.body: Keel registers its webhook subscriptions through the API at connect time against {webhookUrl}. For a custom app the signing secret is the app's API secret key. The endpoint answers 200 within milliseconds, stores the event and processes it in the background; duplicates are ignored by (topic, id, updated_at).

steps.title: Initial import
steps.body: Click Resync: locations, products, inventory and discounts are imported, then orders page by page with a resumable cursor. Large stores continue across several worker runs; progress is visible under “Recent sync runs”.

steps.title: Order state rules
steps.body: Keel never derives the order status from fixed tags. Open Settings → Order states and map the store's tags, payment methods and financial/fulfillment statuses to the canonical states; preview the result on the last 50 orders.

steps.title: Verify
steps.body: Test connection shows the shop name and the granted scopes; place a test order in the store and watch it appear in Orders within seconds, with an “imported” event in its timeline.

steps.title: Public app (optional)
steps.body: Create the app in the Partner dashboard, set the redirect URL to /api/integrations/shopify/oauth/callback, put the client id and secret in SHOPIFY_API_KEY and SHOPIFY_API_SECRET, then use “Install via OAuth”.

errors.fix: The token was revoked or copied incompletely. Create a new token in the app and reconnect.
A scope is missing: the card shows which. Add it in the app configuration and reinstall.
The signing secret differs from the one saved in Keel. Reconnect with the current API secret key.
Normal under heavy sync: Keel waits and retries automatically; the run resumes from its cursor.

meta.title: Connect Meta Ads
meta.intro: Keel reads campaigns and daily insights and can pause or resume campaigns with an explicit confirmation. A system user token keeps the connection alive without personal logins.

steps.title: Create a system user
steps.body: In Business Settings → Users → System users create an Admin system user named “Keel”.

steps.title: Assign the ad account
steps.body: Add assets → Ad accounts → select the account → Manage campaigns (needed for pause/resume) or View performance (read-only).

steps.title: Generate the token
steps.body: Generate new token → choose the app → permissions ads_read, ads_management, business_management → never expires. Copy it once.

steps.title: Connect in Keel
steps.body: Integrations → Meta Ads → Connect: paste the ad account id (act_…) and the token. Test connection shows the account name and granted permissions.

steps.title: Backfill
steps.body: Resync pulls the last 30 days in 7-day windows; the nightly job refreshes the last 3 days because Meta restates recent insights.

errors.fix: Token expired or revoked: generate a new one for the system user.
Rate limit on the ad account: Keel backs off and retries; reduce backfill windows if it persists.
The system user lacks the ad account asset or the permission; fix it in Business Settings.

google.title: Connect Google Ads
google.intro: Read-only in this version: campaigns and daily cost, impressions, clicks and conversions through the Google Ads API.

steps.title: Developer token
steps.body: From a Manager (MCC) account open Tools → API Center and request a developer token; Basic access is enough for production reads.

steps.title: OAuth client
steps.body: In Google Cloud create an OAuth client (Web or Desktop) with the Google Ads API enabled; note client id and secret.

steps.title: Refresh token
steps.body: Authorise the scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords with a user who can access the customer account and keep the refresh token.

steps.title: Connect in Keel
steps.body: Integrations → Google Ads → Connect: customer id (digits), manager id when accessed through an MCC, developer token, client id/secret, refresh token.

steps.title: Verify
steps.body: Test connection runs a one-row GAQL query; Resync imports campaigns and the last 30 days of metrics.

errors.fix: The developer token is not approved for this account, or the login-customer-id is missing for an MCC-managed account.
The refresh token was revoked; authorise again and reconnect.

anthropic.title: Connect the AI assistant (Anthropic)
anthropic.intro: The assistant runs on your own Anthropic API key: Anthropic bills the usage to your account, and Keel only stores the key, encrypted. Without a key the Assistant page asks to connect one.
anthropic.scopes:
No permission scopes: one API key from the store's own Anthropic account.
What is sent to the model: the question, and the figures of the reports the assistant reads to answer (totals, product and campaign names; for customer predictions, customer names and amounts). The assistant can never change data.

steps.title: Create the Anthropic account
steps.body: Go to console.anthropic.com and sign up with a company email. Create the organization in the store's name, so the invoices go to the store.

steps.title: Add credits and a spend limit
steps.body: Settings → Billing: add a payment method and buy credits. Settings → Limits: set a monthly spend limit, so the cost can never surprise you.

steps.title: Optional: a workspace for Keel
steps.body: Settings → Workspaces → Create workspace "Keel". Usage then shows separately in the console, and the workspace can have its own spend limit.

steps.title: Create the API key
steps.body: Settings → API keys → Create key, in the Keel workspace if you made one, named "Keel". Copy it now: the console shows it only once.

steps.title: Paste it in Keel
steps.body: Integrations → AI (Anthropic) → Connect, paste the key, Connect. Keel checks the key by reading the model's details (no tokens spent) and stores it encrypted. "Test connection" repeats the check at any time.

steps.title: Try it
steps.body: Open Assistant and click a suggested question. Under each answer you see the figures with their period and a link to the report. The side panel shows this month's tokens; the same usage appears in the Anthropic console → Usage.

steps.title: Who can use it
steps.body: Every role can ask questions. The assistant only reads the reports the user's role can open, and each user's conversations are private.

errors.fix: The key was copied incompletely, revoked, or belongs to a disabled workspace. Create a new key and connect again.
New Anthropic accounts start with low rate limits, which rise with usage and credits purchased. Wait a minute; if it happens daily, check the limits in the console.

errors.symptom: "Credit balance is too low" in the console, answers failing
errors.fix: Add credits in Settings → Billing, or turn on auto-reload.
Start a new conversation. If it repeats, the model may not be available on the account: check the console.

tracking.title: Activate the pixel and server-side conversions
tracking.intro: The pixel runs on the store; conversions use the Meta and Google connections already in Integrations. No extra credentials are stored for the pixel.
tracking.scopes:
Meta: the system user token needs the dataset (pixel) assigned with Manage access.
Google: a conversion action of type "Import → clicks", and Customer data terms accepted for user identifiers.
Privacy: decide which consent category (marketing or analytics) the pixel runs under.

steps.title: Copy the custom pixel
steps.body: Integrations → Pixel & conversions → copy the Shopify custom pixel. It already contains this store's collect address.

steps.title: Add it in Shopify
steps.body: Shopify admin → Settings → Customer events → Add custom pixel → name it "Keel" → paste the code → Save → Connect.

steps.title: Set the customer privacy permission
steps.body: In the pixel's settings choose the permission that matches your consent policy (Marketing or Analytics). With Shopify's cookie banner the pixel only runs after consent.

steps.title: Check that events arrive
steps.body: Browse the store in a private window, then reload the Pixel & conversions page: events and sessions grow, and an order placed from that window shows its journey. "Send test event" checks Keel's side alone.

steps.title: Meta: dataset and token access
steps.body: Events Manager → Data sources → your dataset (pixel) → copy its id. In Business Settings → System users → Keel → Add assets → Datasets, give it Manage access. Optional: copy a Test event code from Events Manager → Test events to see the first events there.

steps.title: Avoid double counting with Meta
steps.body: If Shopify's Facebook & Instagram app already sends Conversions API events ("Maximum" data sharing), keep only one server source: either turn that off or leave Keel's Meta sending disabled.

steps.title: Google: conversion action
steps.body: Google Ads → Goals → Conversions → New → Import → Other data sources or CRMs → Track conversions from clicks; category Purchase. Copy the conversion action id (ctId in the address bar). Accept the Customer data terms under Goals → Settings to send hashed identifiers.

steps.title: Enable and run
steps.body: Enter the ids, keep "Only customers who accept marketing" unless your legal basis says otherwise, save, then Run queue now. The delivery log shows each order's outcome; the job repeats every 5 minutes.

errors.fix: The custom pixel is not connected, consent was not given in the test browser, or the store origin is not in the allowed list.
The token expired or the system user lost the dataset: generate a new token or reassign the dataset.
The dataset id is wrong, or the event is older than 7 days.
Wrong id, or the action belongs to another account (check the manager account in the Google connection).
Expected when consent is required and customers have not opted in to marketing.

survey.title: Activate the post-purchase survey
survey.intro: A one-question survey ("How did you hear about us?") linked from the order confirmation email. Answers feed the survey-blend attribution model and the Survey tab in Analytics.
survey.scopes: No platform permission: the link is built by the email template with the store's survey secret (Analytics → Survey).

steps.title: Turn the survey on
steps.body: Analytics → Survey → Survey active, adjust the question and option labels in each language, save.

steps.title: Copy the email link
steps.body: The same tab shows the link with this store's secret. It signs the order id with Shopify's hmac_sha256 filter.

steps.title: Add it to the order confirmation
steps.body: Shopify admin → Settings → Notifications → Order confirmation → Edit code. Paste the link where you want the question to appear (after the order summary works well) and save. Send a test email to yourself.

steps.title: Optional: thank-you page
steps.body: A survey block on the thank-you page needs a Shopify checkout UI extension (an app). Until then the email link is the supported path.

steps.title: Read the results
steps.body: Answers appear in Analytics → Survey within seconds. Choose the "Survey blend" model in Attribution to give answered orders' credit partly to the channel customers named.

errors.fix: The template changed the order id (use order.id, not order.name) or the secret was copied incompletely.
The survey is not active.
Move the link higher in the email; one question with big options answers in a second.

email.title: Platform email (Resend)
email.intro: Keel sends sign-in links, invitations, notifications and digests from one platform sender. This guide is for the platform administrator: tenants need nothing.

steps.title: Create the Resend account
steps.body: Sign up at resend.com with the platform administrator mailbox and turn on two-factor authentication.

steps.title: Add the sending domain
steps.body: Domains → Add domain. Use a subdomain dedicated to transactional mail (for example mail.yourdomain.com) and the region closest to your users.

steps.title: SPF
steps.body: Add the MX and TXT records Resend shows for the bounce subdomain (the TXT is an SPF record such as v=spf1 include:… ~all). Keep a single SPF record per name.

steps.title: DKIM
steps.body: Add the DKIM TXT record (resend._domainkey.…) exactly as shown, then wait until Resend marks the domain Verified.

steps.title: DMARC
steps.body: Publish a TXT record on _dmarc.yourdomain.com, for example v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@yourdomain.com. Move to p=quarantine once the reports are clean.

steps.title: Sending-only API key
steps.body: API Keys → Create API key with permission “Sending access”, restricted to the verified domain. It is shown once and starts with re_.

steps.title: Set the Railway variables
steps.body: On the web and worker services set RESEND_API_KEY, EMAIL_FROM (e.g. Keel <no-reply@mail.yourdomain.com>, on the verified domain), EMAIL_REPLY_TO (the support mailbox) and KEEL_INTEGRATION_MODE=live; optionally EMAIL_LEGAL_NAME, EMAIL_LEGAL_ADDRESS and EMAIL_SUPPORT_ADDRESS for the footer. Redeploy. Never commit the key.

steps.title: Delivery webhook
steps.body: Webhooks → Add endpoint {emailWebhookUrl} with the events email.delivered, email.delivery_delayed, email.bounced and email.complained. Copy the signing secret (whsec_…) into RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET on the web service.

steps.title: Send a test email
steps.body: Console → Email must read “Resend is sending”. Send a test email to a mailbox you control, open the original message and check that SPF, DKIM and DMARC pass. The log shows the email as delivered once the webhook arrives.

email.scopes: One API key with “Sending access” only, restricted to the sending domain. Never a full-access key.

errors.fix: RESEND_API_KEY is missing on the service or KEEL_INTEGRATION_MODE is not live: set both and redeploy.
EMAIL_FROM uses a domain Resend has not verified yet: finish the DNS records or use a verified domain.
The key was revoked or has no sending access: create a new sending-only key.
Resend limits requests per second and per day: the queue retries with backoff; upgrade the plan if it persists.
RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET is missing or differs from the endpoint signing secret: the webhook answers 401 or 503.

cod.outcome_description: Every call is an attempt with an outcome. Confirmed moves the order to confirmed; Cancelled cancels it on the platform. Configured tags are written to the platform on every outcome.

outcomes_hint.cancelled: Customer refused: the order is cancelled on the platform

settings.title: COD settings
settings.description: Operators and their hours, scoring weights and thresholds, recipient risk. Nothing here acts automatically on orders: the add-on advises, operators decide.
settings.operators_description: Orders are distributed in proportion to the hours worked today (smooth weighted round-robin). Days off and extra hours override the weekly plan.
settings.weights_description: Relative weights 0–50. A factor with weight 0 is shown but ignored. The score is the weighted mean of the factors that fire, then capped by the recipient risk tier.
settings.risk_description: Returns weighted by age (recent 1.0, older 0.5); one tier of redemption after consecutive deliveries.
settings.recipients_description: Suggestions only: nothing is blocked automatically. Keys are phones or emails, never names.
settings.suggest_blacklist: Suggest blacklist: verify by phone before shipping
settings.suggest_verify: Verify address and intent before shipping
settings.tags_description: How the queue talks to your store through order tags. Nothing is hard-coded: an empty list means that tag flow is not used. Matching ignores case; a trailing * matches a prefix (vendita* matches "Vendita Marco").

tags_read_help.queue: An order carrying one of these enters (or returns to) the queue, whatever its status. Shown on the row and usable to route operators.
tags_read_help.confirmed: Closes the queue item and confirms the order when the tag appears on the platform.
tags_read_help.cancelled: Closes the queue item as cancelled. Precedence: cancelled, then confirmed, then queue.

settings.tags_write_help: Platform first, then Keel: if the store rejects the write, nothing is recorded. Tags already present are not added twice.
settings.tags_clear_on_close: On confirmed and cancelled also remove every queue tag
settings.cancel_restock: Restock lines when an outcome cancels the order

supplier_portal.closed: This order is closed: no answer is needed.
supplier_portal.thanks: Thank you, your answer has been recorded.
supplier_portal.inactive_title: This link is no longer valid
supplier_portal.inactive_body: The link has expired or was replaced by a newer one. Ask the company that sent it for a new link.

planning.title: Inventory planning
planning.description: Forecast, reorder with lead time and safety stock (service level {level}), stock analysis, transfers and purchase cash flow. Review period {review} days.

kpi.urgent_hint: Runs out before the supplier lead time

replenishment.empty_description: Every variant is above its reorder point.
replenishment.created: {n, plural, one {# draft PO created:} other {# draft POs created:}}
replenishment.none_created: No new draft: the selected variants are already in a draft or have no supplier.
replenishment.cover_days: {n} days of cover · lead time {lead} d
replenishment.method: Demand = the higher of the last 90 days' pace and the next two months of forecast. Safety stock = z × √(lead time × σ²demand + demand² × σ²lead time). Order when available + incoming − backorders ≤ reorder point; the quantity covers lead time + review period + safety stock, rounded to MOQ and multiples.

forecast.override_hint: Click a number to correct it; an empty value removes the correction.
forecast.method: Seasonality is learnt on the product type over 24 months, level and trend on the variant (trend capped). Events add their uplift in their month; manual corrections replace the model. Error = WAPE of a forecast made 3 months ago against actual sales.

events.title: Demand events

events.name: Name

kpi.slow_hint: Cover above {days} days or no sales

analysis.matrix_hint: Count and stock value per class. Click a cell to list it.
analysis.legend: ABC ranks by 12-month revenue (80/15/5). XYZ measures demand variability on 4-week buckets (coefficient of variation ≤ 0.5, ≤ 1, > 1).

transfers.empty_description: No location is short while another has surplus.
transfers.hint: Move stock from locations with more than {surplus} days of cover to those with less than {short}. The quantities are written to the commerce platform for both locations.

cashflow.committed_hint: Open purchase orders, net of payments
cashflow.method: Each purchase pays the supplier's deposit when ordered and the balance the agreed days after the expected receipt. Received orders not yet paid fall due from the receipt date.

target.empty_description: The plan scales the forecast mix to the target and shows the stock to buy per variant.

return_policy.title: Return policy and automations
return_policy.description: Rules on top of the default window of {days} days. They apply to the portal and to the team; staff can override with a note.
return_policy.windows_hint: A window applies to items shipped to those countries, of those product types or with those tags (empty = any). When several match, the longest wins; a match replaces the default, also when shorter.

retention.description: Messages to a segment, measured against the segment's control group: what each campaign added over doing nothing.

destinations.title: Live updates and destinations
destinations.description: Push this segment to ad platforms and email tools. Only customers who accept marketing are sent; ad platforms receive hashed identifiers only.
destinations.description_holdout: Push this segment to ad platforms and email tools. Only customers who accept marketing are sent, never the control group; ad platforms receive hashed identifiers only.
destinations.live_help: Re-checked within 10 minutes of any order change, and fully every night (time-based conditions and predictions). Destinations with auto-sync follow.

tracking.title: Pixel and server-side conversions
tracking.description: A first-party pixel on the store feeds multi-touch attribution; confirmed orders go back to Meta and Google from the server, with hashed customer data.

pixel.title: First-party pixel
pixel.description: Sessions, product views, carts and checkouts on the store's own domain. Each session becomes a touchpoint; checkouts and hashed emails link browsers to orders, across visits and devices.
pixel.shopify_help: Paste in Shopify admin → Settings → Customer events → Add custom pixel, then Connect.
